findings.body: The new doc comment states `completion_cost` "fails closed on an unpriced model," but the function (lines 209–216) uses `unwrap_or_else` to bill at `ceiling()` with only a `tracing::warn!`. It returns `f64`, not `Result`, so it cannot fail at all. The module's own existing documentation (lines 17–31) explicitly considered and rejected both "refuse the call" and "refuse at startup," choosing to bill at ceiling instead. The same incorrect claim appears in the test comment for `every_model_the_defaults_select_has_a_price` ("`completion_cost` fails closed on an unpriced model… turns the budget ceiling into a hard error"). A future maintainer reading "fails closed" would expect a hard error where the code silently over-charges, which could mask a stale price table.
findings.title: Correct the "fails closed" claim about completion_cost

value.summary: The PR adds four new model price rows to MODEL_PRICES and four tests covering the new GLM-5.2 pricing and argument ordering. The price math and test assertions are correct. One issue: the new doc comment and test comment both claim `completion_cost` "fails closed" on an unpriced model, but the function actually bills at the ceiling rate with a warning — the same file's module doc explicitly rejected failing as a design choice.
